body:
PROCEDURE: waits and handoffs, shared by Engram and TermAl (rev 7, 2026-10-05; TermAl correction 2026-10-25 below). Rev 6 plus an E3 scope fix from the second dogfood run (Coder, focused run test-83aa52d7), per TermAl src/engram_check_recognition.rs:374-433. CONCURRED by both coordinators: rev 5 at mailbox-ebe242f7 #724/#726, E1-E4 at #731 and #733, the E3 scope fix proposed by Fable2 in #740 and adopted verbatim (#741). TermAl mirrors this text in its own store; any change goes through both coordinators. 2026-10-25 correction (Greg DIRECT, Advisor boundary, TermAl mailbox 63096d00 #75; Engram corrected its copy as rules-waits-and-wakes r8): the Advisor is no longer a recovery owner; it only relays information between Greg and the coordinators.

RULE. Before ending a turn with a dependency outstanding, write a WAIT line and notify its wake owner. A turn boundary, a future credit line or "someone will notice" is not a wake sender. For a boundary-only wait, send the coordinator a final "READY: <exact dependency>"; the coordinator sends the continuation immediately on receipt, even while you're still active. BY is a human coordination deadline, not a host timer. If the recovery owner has no independent wake, write "RECOVERY GAP".

WAIT LINE: a status note on the held item; a mailbox message to the coordinator if no claim is held or the item is already done.
- OWNER: the waiting session.
- ON: the exact dependency identity: run id and directory, delegation and fan-in wait ids, mailbox plus sender plus request message id, or item, run and claim.
- WAKE: the sender and route.
- NEXT: the first action on waking.
- BY: absolute UTC, an estimate agreed by its owner. Without a better estimate, use evaluator 10 min, review pair 20 min, full gate 25 min, focused check 5 min.
- RECOVERY: a named session plus absolute UTC, and what it does.
The note documents the wait; it registers no automatic wake. A status or WAIT note is not a check and does not stale an evaluation.

STANDARD WAITS
1a GATE RESULT. ON: run id, directory and input fingerprint. WAKE: launcher --notify to the coordinator, then the coordinator relays EVERY terminal result, including failure or UNKNOWN, with its fingerprint check; a mismatch is reported, never a reason to withhold the wake. RECOVERY: the coordinator reads the existing run at BY+15 on its next wake and re-sends; it never reruns tests just to get a message. A dead launcher is UNKNOWN until diagnosed. No owner commands or edits during a carried run.
1b HOST CREDIT, after a gate or focused check. ON: the same run plus work, run and claim, awaiting the host verification record or its refusal. A credit line is not a wake: send READY, and the coordinator continues you. NEXT: read the recorded evidence; request evaluation only in a later turn, and only once the record exists. Passing output alone is not credit. If credit stays absent after a relay, report that exact state; it is a recording incident with an owner, not a relay loop. Under the TermAl host (both projects): make no file edits anywhere in the session and run no non-read command in that worktree until the host credit record or its refusal has landed; writes after the launcher finishes still count until the host settles. Then the owner may use its worktree again; the credit record is also needed before requesting evaluation. This applies only to runs the host records as checks: a detached full gate, or a foreground check whose command the host recognises. A detached focused run, or a custom script, is never recorded; there is no credit record to wait for, the 1a relay ends the wait, and such a run earns no credit.
2 GATE QUEUE / LAUNCH NOW. ON: the queued slot, item, prepared root and fingerprint, and the command. WAKE: the coordinator's LAUNCH NOW, sent only after READY. NEXT: that one command, then end under the carried-gate rules. All notes and fixes come before launch. A stale slot goes back to the coordinator.
3 PAIR OR EVALUATOR. ON: both review delegation ids, or the evaluator delegation and attempt, plus the returned fan-in wait id. WAKE: TermAl fan-in to the parent; a failed registration is no fan-in. NEXT: fetch the actual results. RECOVERY: the coordinator at BY+15 sends a mailbox continuation; the parent recovers existing results and never respawns because a delivery failed. A held or attention-required child, or an evaluation for a different attempt or basis, is not a clean result.
4 COORDINATOR RULING, CONCURRENCE OR WINDOW. ON: item, proposed text and request message id. WAKE: the coordinator's reply. An answer of "I need X" replaces the wait with X, its owner and a new BY.
5 PEER REPLY. ON: mailbox, expected sender and request id; a later unrelated message is not the reply. A sleeping waiter cannot re-ping itself, so RECOVERY names an independently waking session or says GAP.
6 FOCUS OR NAMING BINDING. Send "READY: binding only" with the exact item and claim; the coordinator replies at once. NEXT: verify the binding took effect, then retry only the refused operation; never edit or test in the naming turn to work around it. A repeated 409 is diagnosed, not worked around. Focus is a pointer, not ownership.
7 LANDING. The holder owns it until the integration owner accepts; Engram's coder is its own integration owner. ON: commit, base, gate run, pair ids and completion evidence. Engram: install with a backup BEFORE the push. TermAl: the integration owner pushes, verifies the remote, then installs with a backup outside any gate window. In both, the pre-push notice is not a wait. In TermAl only the assigned integration owner pushes; other sessions hand off. The coordinator verifies, then sends "master is X" to every coder waiting on it. RECOVERY: ask the owner for its exact stage, and re-read the actual state before any retry.
8 RESTART (TermAl host). OWNER: the TermAl coordinator, with Engram's. ON: the installed build hash and the fix that running sessions need. WAKE: "restart now" relayed to Greg via Engram::Advisor (relay only); Greg restarts; the coordinator confirms the observed running build and relays resume. BY is a moment both agree, not imposed on Greg.
9 GREG DECISION, RESUME OR PROVIDER PARK. ON: the exact question and Advisor request id, or the parked session and its refusal. WAKE: the Advisor relaying Greg's actual word or Resume (relay only). BY: the next agreed status point. Silence never approves. Credit exhaustion is an external limit, not something to retry.

COORDINATOR DUTIES, on each actual wake: process the mailboxes; inspect assigned waits and sessions; act on overdue or missing WAIT lines, each wake naming the dependency and the next action. No wake storms for parked sessions. A send receipt proves the message was stored, not that the session was admitted or ran; provider, Stop or approval blocks stay visible. Recovery must not form an all-asleep cycle: name the waking checker, or state GAP. The Advisor is NOT the coordinator's recovery owner (Greg DIRECT 2026-10-25): the coordinator's own recovery is the other project's coordinator where both have agreed it for a named wait; otherwise it is stated as RECOVERY GAP.

KNOWN GAP: there is no timer. A BY is checked only when its checker is actually woken. Automation (w-4e75a5319cde, w-3123ce57e780; TermAl w-5043851f081f, w-15acfd0087c2) stays parked until Greg's word.
